LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: POETRY

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How is poetry important in our daily life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication
2. appreciate poetry for self- expression

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: POETRY
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication

What this means
In this part you learn to write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate poetry for self- expression

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate poetry for self- expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate poetry for self- expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate poetry for self- expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry to a partner. (skill: appreciate poetry for self- expression)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate poetry for self- expression.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How is poetry important in our daily life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 7.3.1 Creative Writing: Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write a simple poem using neat and legible handwriting for communication.
5. Be able to: appreciate poetry for self- expression.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
